lesson: Lead Forry mirror: standard line is Spikes, but Hidden Power Forry exists as a lure set. Treat Spikes as DEFAULT, not certain.

Lead Forry mirror: opponent may switch to a Rapid Spinner (Starmie) instead of racing Spikes — preempts opp Spikes by bringing in Spin first. Consider double-switch reads when both leads are Forretress.
Forretress vs incoming Starmie: pivoting to a Snorlax-class attacker is often better than racing Spikes when the opp Spinner is already on the field. The Spikes will get spun anyway.
TWave-Starmie set exists in 1500-elo. When opp's Starmie has 1+ free turn vs a Normal-type incoming, Thunder Wave is strictly better than offensive coverage for stall strategies.
Para'd Snorlax facing Starmie that just TWaved: Lovely Kiss is high-EV but switching back to Forretress is the safer line when you expect opp to also switch to set Spikes. Mutual scout.
HIT: Starmie pivots back to Forretress once the para job is done; the Spikes race resumes. Match: pro pivoted exactly as predicted.
HIT: Forry mirror with revealed pivots, both at 100%, predicted Spikes was correct on p1. Reinforce: in Forry-vs-Forry turn 4 after mutual scouting, Spikes is the standard line.

Forry mirror after p1 has revealed it commits to Spikes-setter role: p2's better line may be pre-Spin via Starmie pivot rather than racing the second Spikes layer (forcing p1 to commit further while p2 keeps Spin live).

Snorlax vs Blissey lead: pivot to a Ground attacker (Rhydon Earthquake) breaks Blissey 2HKO. Setup with Curse is a slower line; aggressive break may be the pro choice when a hard-counter is available on the team.

HIT: Blissey vs Snorlax lead, Toxic is the strong-prior call — Snorlax usually has no recovery in Gen 2 OU, Toxic puts it on an 8-turn timer. Toxic into an incoming Rhydon also lands; only Steel/Poison types are immune.

alternative_hypotheses: Just a scout switch (rejected — Umbreon would not be the scout pick if so; Skarmory or another safer pivot would be used)
Sleep-eat sacrifice (rejected — Umbreon is too valuable defensively to sack to Lovely Kiss when Snorlax could absorb instead)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: Turn 5: Umbreon used Pursuit on Jynx, marked super-effective (Dark vs Psychic), 22% damage. Turn 4: Umbreon ate first Ice Beam at 75%; turn 5 second Ice Beam dropped to 56% but the Pursuit landed. The Pursuit-trap thesis is directly confirmed.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Umbreon is the team's dedicated Jynx Pursuit-trapper. The switch t1 brings the trap into the most common Jynx lead opener (Lovely Kiss). Even if Jynx Ice Beams instead, Umbreon's bulk + Leftovers absorb 2 hits before getting low; Pursuit on the eventual Jynx switch removes the sleeper. Standard Gen 2 OU anti-Jynx package.

lesson: Lead Snorlax vs Jynx with Pursuit-trapper on team: switch IMMEDIATELY to Umbreon/Tyranitar to trap Jynx. Eating 2 Ice Beams (~44%) on the trapper is worth removing Jynx from the game. Lovely Kiss race is the wrong line because both sides can sleep, neutralizing the advantage.

alternative_hypotheses: Just cycling to Spikes setter (rejected — Jynx had a free turn to sleep something; only worth giving up if there's a specific reason)
Anti-Snorlax Self-Destruct fear (low confidence — Self-Destruct turn 1 vs Jynx would be unusual)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: Turn 5: Jynx was Pursuit-trapped anyway (came back turn 3, ate Umbreon's Pursuit at 84% turn 5). So the scout-pivot was correct strategy but the follow-up was bad — bringing Jynx back too early. Turn 12: Cloyster used Spikes, confirming it's the team's Spikes setter (additional value behind the scout-pivot).
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Jynx is uniquely vulnerable to Pursuit (Dark-type STAB hits 4x: Dark>Psychic 2x and STAB 1.5x; not quite 4x but close). Smart opponents bring Pursuit-trappers vs Jynx leads. Switching Jynx out turn 1 scouts the opp; if p1 brings the trapper, Cloyster absorbs the Pursuit instead.

lesson: Lead Jynx vs Snorlax: anticipate Pursuit-trap switch (Umbreon/Tyranitar) from p1; pivot to a bulky resist (Cloyster, Forretress) on turn 1 to scout, bring Jynx back when the trapper is out. Not switching = walking into the trap, losing Jynx for nothing.

alternative_hypotheses: Just avoiding Counter (rejected — if that were the only fear, p1 would Rock Slide instead, which can't be Countered as effectively)
Scout for Bliss's move (rejected — Bliss already revealed Toxic turn 1; nothing more to scout)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: Turn 3: p1 Cloyster used Spikes (layer 1 on p2). Turn 4: p2 Cloyster set their own Spikes; p1 Cloyster used Toxic into the mirror. Turn 5: p2 switched Bengar (Gengar) in and took 12% from Spikes immediately — the hazard cost p2 their first switch-in. The Spikes-race ROI was high.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: p1 traded a free Bliss turn for a Spikes layer. The Cloyster pivot is risky (takes Toxic, has no recovery) but the Spikes layer is permanent until spun. Hazard-race over single-target breaks is a known Gen 2 OU principle on stall vs balanced matchups.

lesson: Rhydon vs Blissey free turn: don't auto-Earthquake. Bliss can't break ANY switch-in for one turn, so the EV-maximizing line is to bring in your Spikes setter (Cloyster) on the free pivot. Setting Spikes during a free Bliss turn buys hazard infrastructure that ticks the opp's entire team. The Earthquake KO is available later when the same matchup recurs.

alternative_hypotheses: Counter for a perceived attacker (rejected — opponent's lead was Snorlax, but switched to Rhydon then Cloyster; the actual attacker hasn't entered)
Sing/Thunder Wave instead (lower-EV — Toxic is permanent damage; sleep wakes up)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: Turn 4: p1 Cloyster at 89% from poison. Turn 5: Cloyster bailed at low HP, never used Surf or any offensive coverage; confirms Cloyster was the setter, not the attacker. Counter would have been wasted (no damage to reflect).
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Bliss's job is to stack poison timers across opp's team. Cloyster has no recovery and is Water/Ice (not Steel/Poison-immune), so Toxic lands and puts it on a ~6-turn clock. Even if p1's Cloyster sets Spikes, it now has to spend turns recovering OR get worn down faster than it can convert. Toxic > Counter when no attacker is incoming.
investigation.set_archetype: Status Blissey (Soft-Boiled + Toxic + Light Screen + filler)

lesson: Blissey's role is status-spreader: Toxic every new switch-in regardless of what they are. Counter is a reactive trap that only fires vs a CONFIRMED attacker. When opp brings in a setter (Cloyster) or wall, Counter is dead weight — Toxic is always live.
HIT: Cloyster vs Blissey, Spikes is correct -- Bliss can't break Cloyster, set hazards while it's safe.

alternative_hypotheses: Soft-Boiled to top off Bliss (rejected: Bliss at 100%, no chip to heal)
Toxic again (rejected: Cloyster already poisoned)
Switch to a wallbreaker (rejected: no offensive piece appropriate t3; setter mirror is the highest-EV pivot)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t4: p2 Cloyster set Spikes layer 1 on p1's side; t5: p2 Cloyster pivoted to Gengar (Hypnosis lead + Destiny Bond trade vs Zap). The Cloyster pivot bought a hazard layer + a setup target for Gengar.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Bliss has no offensive move that pressures Cloyster (Toxic redundant on a Steel/Water-Ice trap target's setter clock, Soft-Boiled gives no chip). Pivoting to own Cloyster begins the Spikes mirror, preserves Bliss for status-spread on later switch-ins.

lesson: Blissey vs opp's Spikes-setting Cloyster: pivot to your own Cloyster (or another setter) to start the hazard mirror. Bliss has no pressure vs Cloyster -- Soft-Boiled is a wasted turn while opp racks layers. Start your own race.

alternative_hypotheses: Spikes layer 2 (predicted, rejected by pro: layer 2 costs HP + a turn; Toxic flips the race instead)
Switch out preemptively (rejected: Cloyster still at 95% with Toxic ticking, has 4-5 productive turns left)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t12: opp Cloyster died from accumulated toxic + Rock Slide pressure; opp never set layer 2. p1 finished the game with a hazard advantage thanks to t4's Toxic.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Toxic'ing the mirror setter puts a permanent 6-turn clock on it. The Spikes race ends because opp Cloyster dies before opp can stack their own layers. You can switch out and come back later for layer 2; opp can't.

lesson: Cloyster mirror after both setters have 1 layer: Toxic the opp Cloyster instead of racing layer 2. Putting the opp setter on the clock decides the race -- opp can't get 3+ layers before it dies. Toxic > layer 2 when the opp is a mirror setter.
HIT: Cloyster mirror, p2 matches p1's layer 1 by setting their own -- standard mirror race line.

alternative_hypotheses: Spikes layer 2 (predicted, rejected: opp Cloyster will switch and Spikes get spun later anyway; preserving Cloyster's HP is higher EV)
Switch to Rhydon (rejected: Rhydon doesn't threaten opp Cloyster the way Zap does -- Earthquake vs Cloyster is good but Rhydon takes Surf in return)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t6-t8: Zapdos pressured Gengar (the opp's pivot in), traded 1-for-1 via Destiny Bond. t11: Cloyster came back with toxic still ticking but contributed a Toxic on Tyranitar. The Zapdos pivot generated 1 KO + scouted opp's Gengar set.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Cloyster's Spikes role is done once both setters are toxic'd and have 1 layer each. Switching to Zapdos preserves Cloyster's clock-HP for later use AND brings in a Tbolt threat against opp Cloyster (and Hypnosis bait for Gengar). Pivot maximizes board pressure.
investigation.set_archetype: Standard Zapdos (Thunder/HP Ice/Thunder Wave/Whirlwind or Drill Peck)

lesson: Cloyster mirror, both toxic'd, layer 1 on each side: pivot to a wallbreaker (Zapdos) instead of racing layer 2. Cloyster's role is done -- preserve its remaining HP for a later layer or Explosion. Bring in the threat that punishes opp's pivots (Zapdos vs Cloyster/Gengar).

alternative_hypotheses: Spikes layer 2 (predicted, rejected: same logic as p1 mirror -- preservation > another layer)
Switch to Blissey (rejected: Bliss can't pressure incoming Zap; Gengar threatens it)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t6-t7: Gengar attempted Hypnosis on Zapdos twice (missed twice); t8: Gengar Destiny Bonded Zap for a 1-for-1 trade. Cloyster returned t11 at full HP, still toxic'd, contributed Toxic on Tyranitar before dying t12 to Rock Slide.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Gengar is the natural Cloyster pivot in Gen 2 OU stall/balance: immune to Normal/Fighting, threatens Hypnosis + Destiny Bond on the predicted Zapdos switch. Preserving Cloyster's toxic clock for a return trip later.

lesson: Cloyster mirror, both toxic'd: pivot Cloyster to Gengar. Preserves Cloyster for later Spikes/Explosion AND brings in a Hypnosis threat that wallpapers any incoming Electric (Zapdos) or Normal attacker. The pivot also forces p1 to commit -- if they bring Zap, Gengar Hypnosis; if they stay, Cloyster mirror at -1 HP.
HIT: Zapdos vs Gengar, Thunder is the play -- STAB chip through Hypnosis risk; max-EV line.
HIT: Gengar vs Zapdos, Hypnosis is the standard Gen 2 OU opener -- sleep the threat to convert.
HIT: Zapdos vs Gengar repeat -- Thunder spam until Gengar breaks; previous Hypnosis miss confirms the line.
HIT: Gengar vs Zapdos repeat -- Hypnosis re-spam after t6 miss; commit to the sleep plan, alternatives are weaker.
HIT: Zapdos vs Gengar at 49% -- Thunder kills; commit to the break.

alternative_hypotheses: Explosion (predicted, rejected: less reliable -- Boom can be switched-into by a Normal/Ghost-resist; Zap can also Whirlwind out of Boom in some sets)
Hypnosis spam #3 (rejected: ~57% accuracy compounded = ~9% the third time lands; trade value > sleep value at 49% HP)
Switch out (rejected: any switch-in eats Spikes and gives Zap a free turn; Gengar's role expires here)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t8: opp Zap Thunder KO'd Gengar; DB triggered; Zap also died. Clean 1-for-1 trade as predicted by the DB plan.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Gengar at 49% on Zap-killable HP, two failed Hypnosis attempts. DB is the safer trade than Boom: DB guarantees the 1-for-1 IF Gengar dies that turn (which opp's Thunder ensures); Boom can be switched-into if opp predicts. Locked Zapdos = perfect DB setup.

lesson: Gengar at ~50% facing a Thunder-locked Zapdos: Destiny Bond is the guaranteed-trade dying play -- locks the KO if opp Thunders. Reach for DB before Explosion when opp's move is predictable and unblocked; Explosion is the alternative when opp has a Ghost-resist switch-in.

alternative_hypotheses: Switch to Rhydon (predicted, rejected: HP Ice is too common on Zap sets at any rating; Rhydon trades down to a guess move)
Stay Vap and Surf (rejected: Vap dies to 2 Tbolts; no win condition vs Zap with Vap active)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t9: Snorlax took Tbolt + para; t10: Snorlax Rested off the para; Snorlax remained alive through midgame as a clock-piece. Rhydon was held in reserve. Confirms preservation thesis.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Rhydon vs unknown Zapdos set is HP-Ice-fragile (4x weak). Snorlax is the safer pivot vs uncertainty -- tanks all of Zap's plausible moves on neutral or near-neutral. Rhydon's role (anti-Electric, anti-Flying) is more valuable preserved for a later threat (e.g., opp Cloyster, opp Tyranitar's Rock Slide).
investigation.set_archetype: CurseLax / Rest Snorlax (clock-piece, not raw breaker)

lesson: Vaporeon vs opp Zapdos: switch to Snorlax over Rhydon. Rhydon is the perfect Thunder switch-in but dies to HP Ice (4x weak); Snorlax tanks both Thunder AND HP Ice on neutral. Preserves Rhydon for the late-game phase where its Ground STAB is needed unblunted. Snorlax also gates the Rest/Belly Drum win condition.

alternative_hypotheses: HP Ice (predicted, rejected: prediction-dependent, only spikes vs Rhydon)
Thunder Wave Vap directly (rejected: TWave wastes the turn if Vap switches; Tbolt para chance is the same EV without the wasted-turn risk)
Switch out (rejected: Zap at 100%, no incoming threat forces a switch yet)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t9: Tbolt hit Snorlax for 25% + paralyzed; t10: para'd Snorlax used Rest to wake up but lost momentum. Para on Snorlax = full-fight tempo gain.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Tbolt's coverage > HP Ice's coverage in this matchup: Tbolt hits Vap stay, Snorlax pivot, Cloyster pivot all reasonably; HP Ice only spikes vs Rhydon (which the cautious opp may withhold). The para chance materialized into a permanent advantage.

lesson: Zapdos vs Vaporeon (after Gengar trade): Thunderbolt is the safer damage option. HP Ice is a 'predict the Rhydon switch' play -- if opp pivots to Snorlax (more common than Rhydon at 1300 elo), HP Ice does little. Tbolt damages stay-in AND the most likely Snorlax/Cloyster pivots, AND the 10% para chance is a free side bet.

alternative_hypotheses: Sleep Powder click (most likely intended move; would have slept Jynx for free turn if accuracy held)
Switch to Pursuit-trapper (predicted, rejected by pro: would lose tempo + reveal Pursuit user prematurely)
Switch to a Spikes setter (rejected: same tempo loss)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t2: pro switched to Raikou (fast Electric breaker) after Exeggutor took 88%+freeze, suggesting the team's Jynx-counter was speed-based, not Pursuit-based. The Pursuit-trap line from the retrieved case did NOT match this team comp.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: At tournament level, the Exeggutor lead is a Sleep Powder / Psychic lead, not a Pursuit-trapper-bait. The team likely has a Pursuit user (Tyranitar) on the bench but uses Exeggutor's speed-control sleep first; the trapper comes in once Jynx is committed.
investigation.set_archetype: Lead Sleep Powder Exeggutor + Raikou breaker (tournament team)

lesson: Lead Exeggutor vs Jynx in tournament play: pro chose to keep Exeggutor in over Pursuit-trap switch. The retrieved case (Snorlax-Jynx Pursuit-trap) over-generalized -- Exeggutor's role isn't to absorb damage for the Pursuit-trapper; it's to Sleep Powder or Psychic the threat. Even with 2x Ice weakness, the Exeggutor stay can be correct when team comp puts Eggy's sleep value > preserved HP. Adjust retrieval: 'lead vs Jynx pivot' lessons are role-dependent (Snorlax-lead pivots, Exeggutor-lead stays).

alternative_hypotheses: Lovely Kiss (predicted, rejected by pro: sleep race vs Eggy's Sleep Powder is even-EV at best; Ice Beam is asymmetric advantage)
Pivot to scout (rejected: free turn vs Eggy's 2x weakness is too valuable to spend)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t1: Ice Beam crit-froze Exeggutor (12% + freeze). t2: opp switched to Raikou, Ice Beam continued to chip (Raikou took 33%). The damage-first plan generated value across two turns.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Ice Beam vs Exeggutor at full HP: 2x effectiveness means 50-70% damage range + 10% freeze chance (which materialized). Forces opp to either switch (Jynx gets free turn vs the switch-in) or stay in nearly KO'd. Lovely Kiss is wasted on Exeggutor since Exeggutor's own Sleep Powder is the parallel threat; a sleep race favors neither side. Direct damage > sleep when opp is Ice-weak.
investigation.set_archetype: Ice Beam-first Jynx (vs Ice-weak leads like Exeggutor, Celebi, Tyranitar opp)

lesson: Lead Jynx vs Exeggutor: Ice Beam is the high-EV punish (2x super-effective + 10% freeze chance) instead of Lovely Kiss. Reasoning: Exeggutor is one of Jynx's best Ice Beam targets in OU; the immediate damage threat (likely 2HKO) + freeze RNG > sleeping into the Pursuit-trapper switch. Lovely Kiss is the play vs neutral targets; Ice Beam is the play vs Ice-weak leads.

alternative_hypotheses: Switch to Tyranitar (predicted, rejected by pro: slow Pursuit-trap is unnecessary when fast counter exists; reveals trapper later as a surprise)
Switch to Cloyster (rejected: doesn't threaten Jynx with KO; just absorbs Ice Beam)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t3: Raikou stayed in for one turn, then p1 double-switched to Cloyster (start the Spikes plan). The Raikou reveal pressured Jynx to pivot (which it did t3, to Snorlax).
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Raikou is a speed-tier counter to Jynx (115 > 95 spe; Thunderbolt 2HKOs Jynx). Pursuit-trap (predicted) preserves a slower piece but loses tempo. Tournament teams often run Raikou as the Jynx answer alongside Pursuit users, choosing per-game which to reveal. This game: Raikou first.

lesson: Frozen Exeggutor at 12%: switch to a SPEED-counter (Raikou outspeeds Jynx) rather than the Pursuit-trapper. Raikou-class breakers threaten Jynx with KO via Thunderbolt while shrugging Ice Beam (neutral). Pursuit-trap is the slow line; speed-tier counter is the fast line. Both valid -- pick by team comp.

alternative_hypotheses: Switch out (predicted, rejected: spends Jynx's tempo for scouting info that's already inferable -- opp's next mon must be a Jynx counter)
Lovely Kiss (rejected: Eggy already frozen; LK can't stack)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t2: Ice Beam hit incoming Raikou for 33%; that damage compounded across the game (Raikou had to be played carefully throughout).
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Frozen Exeggutor will switch (no point staying frozen); Jynx's free turn is best spent damaging the switch-in. Pivot-to-scout costs Jynx's tempo; Ice Beam captures it. The retrieved case (scout pivot) over-generalized: scout pivots are correct vs full-HP active threats, not vs already-broken leads.
investigation.set_archetype: Ice Beam Jynx (commit to damage when opp is already broken)

lesson: Jynx vs frozen Exeggutor: pro chose Ice Beam over the predicted scout-pivot. Free turn vs frozen = free damage on the inevitable switch-in. The retrieved 'pivot to scout' case applies vs uncommitted leads, not vs already-broken leads.

alternative_hypotheses: Thunderbolt (predicted, rejected: only hits Jynx, who's pivoting anyway -- damage doesn't translate to board state)
Stay Raikou and Crunch (rejected: same issue as Tbolt; Raikou's role is anti-Jynx, not breaker)
Switch to Spikes setter directly (this IS the action; predicted as 'move' rather than 'switch' is the miss)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t3: simultaneous switch -- p1 Cloyster, p2 Snorlax. t4 (from t5 prompt's revealed moves on Cloyster): Cloyster set Spikes. The double-switch worked perfectly -- p1 got a free Spikes layer on p2's side while p2 spent a turn on the pivot.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: When opp is forced to switch (outsped + damage-threatened), the high-EV move isn't to chip them -- it's to gain board state. Cloyster pivots in to set Spikes vs whatever opp brings (Snorlax can't break Cloyster). The double-switch logic: both sides committed to pivots; pro reads it and brings the highest-value pivot (Cloyster's Spikes role).
investigation.set_archetype: Spikes Cloyster + double-switch tempo (tournament-level pivot timing)

lesson: Raikou vs Jynx at 73%: double-switch to Cloyster instead of Tbolt-attacking. Reasoning: pro reads that Jynx will pivot (it's outsped, can't race Tbolt); both pivot at once. Cloyster comes in vs the unknown switch-in (Snorlax), ready to Spikes if safe. Tbolt would only hit the dead-weight Jynx as it pivots out.

HIT (class): Jynx vs Raikou pivots out -- predicted switch-out class was correct. Specific mon chosen by pro: Snorlax (Tbolt-tank + Curse/Belly Drum win-condition). Cloyster would also be valid (Tbolt-resist 0.5x + Spikes setter); Forretress also valid. Snorlax favored by pros for its setup potential.

alternative_hypotheses: Sleep Powder (predicted, rejected: redundant with Jynx Lovely Kiss for sleep clause)
Switch out (rejected: Eggy lead's role is to status the opp lead, eating the HP hit)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t1: Stun Spore missed but the intent was para. Later turns: pro pivots Eggy around Spore/Stun Spore landings; doesn't reveal Sleep Powder. Set is Stun Spore over Sleep Powder.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Sleep clause limits 1 sleeping mon per side. If team has Jynx (or another sleeper), Eggy runs Stun Spore to avoid sleep-clause conflict. Para Raikou removes its speed advantage (no longer outspeeds slower offense) and halves Atk.
investigation.set_archetype: Stun Spore Exeggutor (status-spreader; team likely has Jynx as sleeper)

lesson: Lead Exeggutor vs Raikou: Stun Spore over Sleep Powder when team has another sleeper (e.g. Jynx). Para is permanent + halves Atk and Speed; Sleep wakes up. Pick Stun Spore when Eggy is the team's status-piece, not its sleeper.

alternative_hypotheses: Crunch (predicted, rejected: only 2x SE; HP Bug is 4x SE on same target)
Thunder Wave Eggy (rejected: para Eggy has minor effect since it's slow anyway)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t1: HP did super-effective damage (42% to Eggy at full HP). The damage rolls match a 4x SE HP Bug hit (a 2x Crunch would do ~30%).
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: HP Bug is Raikou's signature Hidden Power type in Gen 2 OU because it 4x-hits Celebi AND Exeggutor (both Grass/Psychic). Crunch is 2x via Dark>Psychic only; HP Bug stacks the Grass weakness for 4x total. The pro's Raikou set is HP Bug (anti-Celebi/Eggy variant), not HP Ice (anti-Salamence variant).

lesson: Raikou vs Exeggutor lead: Hidden Power Bug (4x SE; Bug 2x vs Grass and 2x vs Psychic) is the anti-Celebi/Exeggutor signature move. Crunch (predicted) hits Eggy 2x via Dark>Psychic but ignores the Grass 2x. HP Bug Raikou is the OU staple for breaking Grass/Psychic walls.

alternative_hypotheses: Stun Spore re-click (predicted, rejected: 25% miss rate compounds; Raikou expected to pivot)
Giga Drain (rejected: Raikou neutral to Grass; insufficient damage)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t2: simultaneous double-switch (p1->Snorlax, p2->Skarmory). t3: third double-switch in a row. Tournament-level early game is dominated by tempo pivots, not stay-in trades.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: After Stun Spore miss + 42% HP loss, Eggy is on a clock. Pivoting to Snorlax sets up the SnoLax Curse/Rest win condition AND preserves Eggy for a fresher matchup later. Predict-pivot expects opp Raikou to also pivot (Raikou doesn't want to eat a successful Stun Spore re-click).

lesson: Exeggutor 64% vs Raikou 100% after t1 trade: pivot Eggy out to Snorlax (Tbolt-tank) rather than re-clicking Stun Spore. Reasoning: opp will likely switch out of Eggy stay-in (revealed Stun Spore threat); pivot Eggy preserves the status-piece for later. Double-switch tempo.

alternative_hypotheses: HP Bug re-click (predicted, rejected: only useful if Eggy stays; predict-pivot wins)
Crunch (rejected: same issue, useful only on stay-in)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t2: simultaneous double-switch confirmed; p1 brought Snorlax (Tbolt-tank). t3: another double-switch. Skarmory pivot was correct.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Raikou has revealed HP Bug to opp; opp will pivot Eggy out and bring a Raikou-check (Snorlax tanks Tbolt; Rhydon Earthquake Raikou; Ground/Bulky). Skarmory is the safe pivot vs unknown switch-in: resists most threats, sets Spikes later.
investigation.set_archetype: Skarmory Spikes setter (pivots-in vs unknown breaker)

lesson: Raikou vs damaged Eggy 64%: pivot Raikou out to Skarmory rather than re-click HP Bug. Reasoning: read p1's Eggy pivot (likely to bring in a Raikou-counter). Skarmory comes in fresh to absorb whatever p1 brings (Tbolt-resist Steel/Flying; tanky generally).

alternative_hypotheses: Body Slam (predicted, rejected: 0.5x damage; para chance moot vs Skarm; Skarm pivots out anyway)
Curse (rejected: Skarm Whirlwinds; setup wasted)
Self-Destruct (rejected: premature; Skarm tanks Boom on resist)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t3: simultaneous double-switch (third in a row); p2 brought Misdreavus (Ghost-type, immune to Body Slam). Body Slam would have done 0 damage; pivot was correct.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Snorlax can't break Skarmory (Body Slam 0.5x via Steel; Skarm immune to Lax's EQ via Flying). Staying gives Skarm a free Spikes turn. Pivoting to Zapdos: trades a Spikes layer for Zap-pressure on the rest of opp's team. Zap also resists Drill Peck (Flying vs Flying = neutral, but Zap's bulk is high enough).

lesson: Snorlax vs Skarmory: pivot to Zapdos rather than Body Slam-chipping Skarm. Reasoning: Skarmory will Spikes; pivoting now eats one Spikes layer for free + brings in Zapdos (immune to Skarm's Drill Peck, threatens with Thunder on the predicted Skarm pivot OR opp's next mon).

alternative_hypotheses: Spikes (predicted, rejected: stay-in only gains value if opp stays; predict-pivot wins)
Whirlwind (rejected: phazes random, but doesn't extract setup value)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t3: simultaneous double-switch (third!); p1 brought Zapdos. Misdreavus vs Zapdos forces another pivot decision (Zap doesn't want to be Mean Looked + Perish Song'd).
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Spikes is the standard move but pro reads the predict-pivot. Pivoting to Misdreavus brings a status/trapper that threatens many switch-ins (Mean Look + Perish Song trap; Thunder Wave; Pain Split sustain). Tempo > Spikes when both sides are pivoting.
investigation.set_archetype: Mean Look + Perish Song Misdreavus trapper

lesson: Skarmory vs Snorlax: pivot to Misdreavus rather than Spikes. Reasoning: Snorlax will pivot too (Lax can't break Skarm); preempting with own pivot brings in Misdreavus to threaten the incoming. Misdreavus is Ghost-type, immune to Normal moves (Lax's Body Slam) and Fighting; with Mean Look + Perish Song trap potential.

HIT (class): Zapdos vs Misdreavus pivots out. Misdreavus runs Mean Look + Perish Song -- Zap stays in eats a 3-turn KO trap. Specific pivot: back to Exeggutor (the team's status piece; threatens Sleep Powder/Stun Spore on Misdreavus). Cycles back to t1 matchup (Eggy vs Raikou after p2's Raikou pivot).

alternative_hypotheses: Mean Look (predicted, rejected: only fires on stay-in; pro reads pivot)
Perish Song uncommitted (rejected: same issue; pivot wins)
Thunder Wave Zap (rejected: less committal but still requires stay-in)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t4: simultaneous double-switch (FOURTH in a row); p1 brought Eggy back, p2 brought Raikou back. Same matchup as t1. Tempo battle continues.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Mean Look only works if opp stays; pivoting takes the tempo gain (Raikou pressures the predicted Eggy switch-back with HP Bug 4x). Misdreavus preserved for a future trap window on a committed mon (e.g., setup'd Snorlax).

lesson: Misdreavus vs Zapdos: pivot to Raikou rather than Mean Look + Perish. Reasoning: Zapdos will pivot (Mean Look fear); committing to Mean Look only fires on a stay-in. Pivot Misdreavus, bring Raikou to threaten the incoming (likely Eggy back) with HP Bug 4x.

alternative_hypotheses: Thunder Wave (predicted, rejected: lower expected value; pro picks max-EV)
Switch out (rejected: gives Lax free Curse turn)
Drill Peck (rejected: weaker than Thunder vs Lax; no para chance)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t1: Thunder missed; pro stayed in t2 and Thunder'd again -- this time hit AND para'd Lax. The risk paid off on t2. t3: pro pivoted to Steelix (anti-CurseLax pivot). t4: Steelix Curse'd -- starting own setup vs neutered Lax.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Tournament-tier pros pick max-EV over max-safety in lead matchups. Thunder's 70% accuracy is offset by the 30% para chance built into Thunder's secondary effect AND the immediate damage. TWave is +EV-safe but lower expected value (no damage, just status). The pro reads that Lax will Curse on the first turn (predictable opening) -- Thunder threatens to break Curse setup AND para Lax simultaneously.
investigation.set_archetype: Aggressive Zapdos (Thunder/HP Ice/Thunder Wave/Whirlwind or Drill Peck) — leads with Thunder pressure

lesson: Lead Zapdos vs Snorlax: Thunder over Thunder Wave. Reasoning: Thunder has secondary 30% para chance + 60% damage to Lax IF it hits (70% acc). The expected value of Thunder = 0.7 * (chip + para chance) > 1.0 * (just para). The pro chooses the higher-variance, higher-EV line at tournament level. Thunder Wave is the safer play; Thunder is the high-EV play.

investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Zap can't reliably break Lax (Thunder ~50% to break in 4-5 hits, even faster Tbolt is similar). Lax with Rest cycle is unkillable by Zap. Free Curse t1 establishes the wincon path: boosted Lax sweeps late-game once support pieces (Skarmory/Steelix) wall Zap. Body Slam chip would do ~30% but gives up the boost.

lesson: Snorlax vs Zapdos lead: Curse over Body Slam. Reasoning: Zap can't break Lax through Rest cycle; first turn is FREE Curse boost (Zap will likely Thunder or TWave -- both pressure Lax but don't 1HKO). +1 Atk +1 Def Lax becomes a 6-turn win condition. Tournament-level: lead Lax goes for setup, not chip.

alternative_hypotheses: Switch to Skarmory (predicted, rejected: premature pivot; gives Lax a free Curse)
Thunder Wave (rejected: para alone doesn't damage; Thunder does both)
investigation.future_turn_evidence: t2: Thunder hit + para'd Lax (the high-EV outcome materialized). t3: pro NOW pivoted (to Steelix) once Lax was neutered by para. The pivot is the FOLLOW-UP, not the first response.
investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: Switch-to-Skarmory walls Lax but yields ZERO pressure on Lax (Lax keeps Cursing). Thunder spam puts Lax on a clock: each hit chips + each landing risks para. The EV calculation: 2 Thunders = ~1 hit + ~1 para landing on average; far better than 0 chip and unlimited Lax setup. Pivot becomes correct AFTER Lax is para'd / chipped enough that Steelix or Skarm can clean up.

Pivoting to Skarmory gives Lax a free Curse 2 turn. Tournament-level: commit to the Thunder gamble until Lax is broken or para'd; switch only after pressure established.

Steelix Curse turns the matchup into 'Steelix wincon vs Lax-can't-break-Steelix' -- a guaranteed win path. Roar is the safer move; Curse is the wincon move.

Double-Edge damages opp NOW, accepts 25% recoil, denies Steelix free setup. CurseLax-with-recoil is a known faster-winning variant than Curse/Rest (sacrifices longevity for damage commit).

lesson: CurseLax para vs Steelix: Double-Edge chip over Rest. Reasoning: Rest cures para but Steelix uses the 2-turn-sleep window to setup further. Double-Edge is the immediate damage commit -- 25% recoil to Lax in exchange for chip on Steelix (resisted but still chip). Tournament-level: pick damage commit when opp is also setting up.
